question.leadin: This group was opposed by an organization called the Lizard League. which has nothing to do with any insane modern conspiracy theories.
question.text: Name this Christian order of crusading knights, who converted the Baltic countries to Christianity. They were defeated by the forces of Wladyslaw II Jagiello (vwah-DEE-swahf "the second" yah-GYEH-woh) at the Battle of Grunwald.
question.answerHtml: Teutonic Order [or the Teutonic Knights, or the Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem]
question.clue: A force from this group fought at the Battle of Legnica against the Mongols.

swap.leadin: Leaders of this movement included John Calvin and Ulrich Zwingli.
swap.text: Name this 16th-century movement that split Protestant groups away from the Roman Catholic Church.
swap.clue: The Council of Trent codified the "Counter-" response to this movement, whose early proponents criticized the sale of indulgences.

question.leadin: This structure was erected in 1961 to enclose the western half of its namesake German city.
question.text: Identify this structure whose demolition began in a public demonstration in 1989. Its destruction symbolized the fall of the Soviet-led Eastern bloc.
question.clue: The construction of this object created "ghost stations" in which subways on certain lines would not stop.

swap.leadin: This city's Burgerbraukeller was the site of an uprising on November 8th, 1923 supported by Erich Ludendorff.
swap.text: Name this Bavarian city, the site of Adolf Hitler's failed Beer Hall Putsch.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.leadin: This organization fought a successful war against Denmark, and also faced the band of pirates known as the Victuals Brothers.
question.text: Name this confederation of German cities, with capital at Lubeck, that included cities like Hamburg and Visby.
question.clue: Members of this organization were expelled from their kontor at Novgorod by Ivan the Terrible.

swap.text: This final president of the republic allowed the Nazis to take power in 1933 by suspending civil liberties after the Reichstag Fire and transferring power to the cabinet with the Enabling Act.
swap.clue: This man was reviled by Hitler, who referred to him as "that old fool" and "that old reactionary" during his time as president of the Weimar ] Republic.

question.leadin: In one speech, this man said that the "great questions of the day" would be decided "Blood and Iron."
question.text: Name this "Iron Chancellor" of Prussia. He heavily edited the Ems dispatch to provoke war with France and was the main force behind German unification in the second half of the 19th century.
question.answerHtml: Otto von Bismarck (or Otto Eduard Leopold, Prince of Bismarck, Duke of Lauenburg)
question.clue: Count Vincent Benedetti delivered a message actually created by this man, and he had the May Laws implemented to supervise Catholic clergy as part of his Kulturkampf.

swap.text: In this 1923 incident, Hitler and Ludendorff attempted to gain control by attacking the namesake structure in Munich, with the help of the SA.
swap.clue: In the aftermath of this event, Georg Neithardt sentenced its main perpetrator to only 8 months in prison after being impressed by his oratory skills, which led to Erich Ludendorff's acquittal.

question.leadin: Name these questionable items of correspondence from European history.
question.text: This falsified transcript of a meeting between Kaiser Wilhelm I and French ambassador Benedetti enraged France into war with Prussia.
question.clue: During this event, "aide-de-camp" was rendered as "non-commissioned officer", an insult to Count Benedetti, who had been told by the Duke of Gramont to ask about the candidate chosen by Juan Prim for the Spanish throne.

swap.leadin: This monarch's many unwise remarks included calling the English "mad as march hares" in a Daily Telegraph interview.
swap.text: Name this monarch whose navy was built up rapidly by Alfred von Tirpitz. The General Staff of this monarch's army was led by Moltke the Younger.
swap.answerHtml: Kaiser Wilhelm II [or Emperor William II of Germany]
swap.clue: This monarch's naval squadron based at Kiautschou ("k'YAO-choh") was unable to stop Sadakachi Kato's naval bombardment during the siege of Tsingtao ("ching-DAO"), resulting in the loss of an overseas concession.

question.text: This was the name given to various German encryption machines during World War II. In a major boost for the Allies, British codebreakers, using intelligence code-named Ultra, broke the codes created by this machine.
question.clue: This device was combated by the bombe, a form of early computer.

swap.text: Among the various construction projects that Ludwig undertook was this castle, which is located close to the Hohenschwangau Castle where Ludwig grew up. Ludwig was inspired by the Singers' Hall of Wartburg Castle when cooking up his plans for this castle.

question.text: The Germans achieved success near the end of the War by using these troops to break the trench stalemate. Oskar von Hutier pioneered their tactics, which were used to great success during the Ludendorff Offensive.
question.answerHtml: stormtroopers [or stoßtruppen; sturmmann; sturmtruppen; prompt on translations like shock troops or assault troops]
question.clue: German victory at Caporetto was partially due to the use of these soldiers. These units used "infiltration tactics" to overwhelm enemy trenches, and their name in German roughly translates as "shock troops."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of printed books.
swap.text: Everyone loves this inventor of the movable type printing press, who printed a namesake version of the bible from his workshop in Mainz.
swap.clue: This man's invention of hand molds and an oil-based substance helped him create his most well-known invention.

question.leadin: A planned merger of this financial institution with one of its main domestic rivals, Commerzbank, fell through in April of 2019.
question.text: Name this financial institution that was one of the key drivers of the collateralized debt obligation market in the lead-up to the 2008 financial crisis, paying major fines for its creation of CDOs like Gemstone VII ["seven"].

swap.leadin: Name these powerful women in 19th-century Europe.
swap.text: This mistress of King Ludwig of Bavaria sought to limit the power of the Jesuits and ultramontanists, but fell from grace in the student revolutions of 1848.
swap.answerHtml: Lola Montez [accept either underlined name; or Marie Dolores Eliza Rosanna Gilbert]
swap.clue: When asked by a European monarch "Nature or art?", she cut open her blouse with a stiletto.

question.leadin: During the Thirty Years War, a Spanish campaign gave control over this state to the Catholic Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria, who returned control over its Rhenish territories in the Peace of Westphalia.
question.text: Name this electoral state in southern Germany that became a center of early Calvinism under a branch of the Wittelsbach dynasty. While ruling this state, Frederick V formed the Protestant Union before the Thirty Years War.
question.answerHtml: Electoral Palatinate [or the Electorate of the Palatinate; accept Kurpfalz or Kurfürstentum Pfalz]

swap.leadin: Targets of this event included its namesake, who was nicknamed "The Harpist," and General Kuno Graf von Moltke, who was called "Sweetie."
swap.text: Name this 1907 affair centering on accusations by a journalist about the homosexuality of members of Kaiser Wilhelm II's inner circle.
swap.clue: Kuno von Moltke was one of several advisors to Wilhelm II who were accused of being practicing homosexuals during this affair, which rocked pre-WWI Germany.

question.text: Albert Speer and this man were the last two inmates to be released before Hess. He was the head of the Hitler-Jugend, or Hitler Youth from 1933 forward.

swap.leadin: This polity came under the rule of the Franconian Hohenzollerns in 1415, after which it eventually came to dominate the Duchy of Prussia.
swap.text: Name this polity corresponding to a modern German state surrounding Berlin. It lends its name to a famous neoclassical Gate in that city.
swap.answerHtml: Margraviate of Brandenburg [Also accept March of Brandenburg or Electorate of Brandenburg.]
swap.clue: The portion of this polity east of the Oder-Neisse line is the Neumark, which was transferred to Poland following World War II.
